title: M7.P5: Replace automatic cloud migration with explicit folder setup
body:
## Source integration published — 2026-10-08

Product `e6645cb5ea5ae3c7f699390a74b22d098fbeb7fb` and proof `bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3` are on next; ES4e410dc9 is published and pinned. #515's finite instructions-only relocation disposition and fixes #520/#521/#522/#523 are qualified and closed. [Exact inputs and proof](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-save-repair-cases) include host controls, affected cloud UI and actual native screenshot/backup/restore, complete preservation manifests and completed scratch retirement.

Remaining order: #507 frozen independent audit, engineering GENERIC_X64 image, CF10 clean/public ROCKNIX adoption and actual inclusion; then affected H700 followed by SM8550 builds and release gates. This issue remains open for those assembled-image criteria. No personal/cloud action or RC claim follows from source integration; #519 separately gates the owner's next transfer/reboot. The earlier sections below retain the implementation/qualification history; their in-progress source observations are superseded by this status.

## Current scope — post-connection setup, not automatic cloud migration

D-CLOUD-175/177/178/179 retire the automatic move/follow/startup migration and optional whole-folder tidier. #510 holds the settled contract; #515 owns concrete progress-file repairs. This issue owns coordinated product integration and final clean/public-adoption proof. No further overall design choice is awaited from the owner.

## Ordered implementation path — M7.P5

1. **#510 — settled contract and reference alignment.** Link/retain the remote, then offer category checks, selected folder creation and instructions. Preserve independent paths. D-CLOUD-178/179 settle this; do not ask the owner to choose the overall design again.
2. **#515 — targeted save-folder repair cases and qualification (next implementation task).** Read public ROCKNIX filters/config and actual emulator writers; distinguish valid layouts from source-proven misplaced saves/states/screenshots. Define exact plans, bounds, collision/source-retention and consent; implement and prove supported actions. Unsupported/ambiguous cases retain instructions. If no safe automatic case exists, retain the case evidence and explicit disposition; never claim an unimplemented repair passed or silently drop a demonstrated requested case.
3. **#508 — coordinated final integration and pins.** Include the qualified foundation and #515's result, remove automatic move/follow and startup/tidy paths, and retain public config/credential preservation. Carry canonical references and proof with the source.
4. **#507 — freeze and independently audit the resulting P5 delta.** Required primary and cross-lab stages; no replay of the accepted candidate16 audit.
5. **#508/#492/#344/#265/#359 — assembled firmware and release gates.** Build the engineering image required for CF10 clean/public ROCKNIX adoption, map final inputs/inclusion, then finish source/licences and named physical/release gates. Source-overlay proof does not establish an installed RC.

**Parallel #511:** setup, ROM and BIOS guides and later verified QR destinations. Local instructions work without the website. The separate Herdr lane still awaits its startup trust answer; it is not a firmware gate.
## Current qualification

The check/create/instructions foundation has completed [source-overlay proof](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/d5e2f78618624cad919afaba6784bef3f7eaf8c7/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-cloud-validator/ui/README.md) at distribution `6f89bc7cecee5972909828103689e2c7c0711c30` and ES `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. Both product branches remain local/unintegrated; the product pin is unchanged. #512/#513/#514 are qualified source fixes and closed; their firmware inclusion belongs to #508.

Evidence: 21 restore controls, 30 validator controls, 1,311 top-level host PASS (zero FAIL/SKIP), ordinary VM WebDAV and SFTP 108 PASS each; 99 UI-index entries comprising 89 reviewed frames, nine rejected frames retained and CF10 assembled firmware/public adoption pending. #512 unit logic passed 183 cases/4,752 assertions; later text-only fixes have separate compile/link/syntax/catalog/vocabulary proof. All owned runtimes are retired and 529 sealed files retained. Accepted candidate16/device artifacts and the 78-frame firmware baseline are unchanged. No build, VM or audit job is running in this lane.

## Resulting behavior and upgrade boundary

Linking or retaining an rclone remote opens the post-connection setup surface. It offers read-only category checks, separately confirmed selected-category CREATE FOLDERS, independent saves/settings/content paths and instructions. Linking alone creates nothing; a folder choice does not relocate files. Fresh defaults use `/pixelelated/Saves`, `/pixelelated/Backups` and `/pixelelated/Content`. ROM/BIOS population or reorganization is manual; supported bounded progress repairs are separate #515 actions.

Preserve credentials and configured paths from public ROCKNIX release20261001/tag `c445081a59518f37d9776e5412dd7b14910696f7`, including `/GAMES`, nested `/GAMES/backup` and explicit custom paths. Normal sync, selective content/settings backup/restore and supported-format guards remain. No automatic ancestor/account-root discovery may adopt another library. An owner-reset experimental cloud is not the public upgrade seed and cannot establish reset local pointers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Final source/install/ES call-site sweep proves there is no installed automatic migration engine, legacy autojoin/follow, startup migration prompt or TIDY move action; syntax/package/catalog checks pass. Local draft evidence exists; integrated source/install inclusion is still required.
- [ ] Synthetic clean linking creates nothing; separately confirmed selected-category CREATE FOLDERS creates only the chosen folders/notes and preserves other trees. Source-overlay before/after hashes/pointer receipts pass; assembled-image CF10 proves the final firmware.
- [ ] Public ROCKNIX configurations retain credentials, independent pointers and cloud bytes through adoption/scans/setup unless explicit selection changes a pointer. Clean installs are proved separately. Unpublished experimental states do not add compatibility requirements.
- [ ] Final firmware's validation and restore discovery stay within selected roots; ordinary save/settings/content, partial-library restore and missing/unreadable/supported-format handling retain their applicable controls. Unchanged tests keep their exact input identity; changed inputs receive affected proof.
- [ ] #515's supported case/action or evidence-backed instructions-only disposition is explicitly mapped to the integrated source and #507 scope. Each implemented repair has consent, bounded transport, collision/stale/interruption/refusal proof and leaves ROMs/BIOS/unknown files untouched.
- [ ] Canonical menu/IA/flow and reviewed EN/FR640×480/1280×800 affected frames match final source; current source-overlay proof is complete above. Any added repair screen requires its own frames. No dead QR destination ships.
- [ ] New full pins/package installation and final artifact inclusion are mapped; source-overlay results are never called installed release firmware. CF10 and final inclusion remain open until an engineering image supplies proof.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: source-derived synthetic fixtures and disposable GENERIC_X64 guests cover setup, repair boundaries, pointers, selective restore, UI and clean/public adoption. No personal-cloud mutation or physical-device action is needed. Reuse already qualified unchanged inputs; do not repeat completed suites without a changed input, failure or unresolved concern.

## Verified history (not current behavior)

The unmerged September29 PRs ROCKNIX/distribution#3404 (`4c83ebede4`) and ROCKNIX/emulationstation-next#40 already contained optional `/GAMES`→`/ROCKNIX` tidying, including derived content moves. Startup autojoining/following came later. The retired engine could copy/check/delete through the handheld on hashless backends; it was not a rename-only operation. #505's extra migration diagnostic draft is isolated and closed not planned. Prior failed/accepted proofs remain historical; they do not authorize reintroducing that flow.

The [canonical review](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/next/docs/pixelelated/cloud-folder-flow-review.md) records the source inventory, implemented flow, prospective repair branch and current evidence. Earlier issue-body snapshots are retained in the 2026-10-08 cloud-plan reconciliation record; obsolete active-job or pending-design statements are superseded by this body.

## Owner-managed alignment and separate private review

The owner reports manually resetting the experimental cloud state and has requested read-only verification plus a later one-time residue review. #516 owns that private operational task, outside M7. Exact account history, timestamps, paths and object inventory remain restricted locally; the tracker records redacted conclusions only.

The report is not verified transfer integrity and does not establish reset device pointers. A later device test uses the new post-connection flow and named action authority; it does not resume the retired automatic migration. No move, deletion, sync or credential export is authorized by the read-only review. Public ROCKNIX/clean qualification uses independent synthetic fixtures and does not wait for personal cleanup.

## Maintainer requirements (preserved verbatim)

> Sounds good, and we should trigger a new lane if you want, within Herdr, for website work. I want to keep us focused here in this lane on the critical path of getting the build completed. We were in the flow, trying to get everything done. Run the changes and adjustments for the release candidate to simplify the experience and expectations of what happens when connecting a new remote via rclone, and I don't want to lose that progress and momentum.

> yes, please do. if we're moving this many files, we should make sure the user knows that they can resume the migration and that no files have been lost and that the integrity of the transfer will be double-checked once it is complete.

> also, we should consider if this is an ineffective process for large libraries. for example, some of my roms are gigabytes big. also, not everyone will have synced everything for that device, so we might wind up confusing users. would a rename be simpler? also, no one has used my fork yet except me, so I'm really the only person migrating. if this is the case, maybe we can take a simpler route? for example, maybe we should just let the user go through the standard new rclone backend link flow to create the `/pixelelated` directory and stub directories, and then they handle the migration?

> I'm fine doing a rename on my end, and then we can abandon the migration entirely, or at least I think we can. I don't think we have an existing cloud migration path for ROCKNIX users that were going to switch to our newer cloud backend configuration, did we? I thought we were just creating the directory structure and then letting them populate it.

> if that's the case, we could access Dropbox directly from this machine and clean everything up in Dropbox without having to go through the handheld.

> Also, with the "tidy up your cloud folders," that only mattered once they'd linked a cloud backend. We should respect their choice in doing that. If they happen to choose a different folder, I didn't think we would move their ROMs around. If we need to add more clarity to our own flows and what tidying up is, we should think more about that. Moving around ROMs, as we found, can be a very data-intensive operation, and so we might want to delineate between organizing or moving ROMs versus all of the other files we deal with. We're not finding ourselves in a situation where we're trying to use a handheld with a limited CPU to move hundreds of GB of files.

> I think we arrived at a good solution for this. I want to make sure everything we had is well documented, put into issues, and that we have a clear implementation path around using our project management methodology.
>
> I feel like we arrived at a good solution that relied on post-rclone remote setup. At the time, verification, directory creation, and user actions could live, so someone could help tidy up certain elements while we provide documentation for how to handle more data-intensive operations.
>
> This would also mean refactoring and redoing what we had done around the initial upgrade path, but I'm fine manually aligning myself with our new framework and directory structure. I can also revert the changes we made in Dropbox and then simply retitle the directory on my end.

## Adoption verification lesson from #517

D-CLOUD-181: remote rollback/rename does not reset client state, and replacement firmware preserves stored configuration. In the existing synthetic adoption proof, verify local category pointers, automatic-sync choices and the absence of retired migration consumers separately from cloud contents. The old pending migration record is not itself a universal sync inhibitor. Do not infer that cloud byte integrity requires replacing local game saves; compare within the actual allowlist and preserve recovery copies.

Use the scoped protocol and failure controls in `docs/cloud-save-integrity.md` where relevant. These are synthetic acceptance refinements, not a personal-owner compatibility feature or a change to M7 priority order.

## Before the owner test handheld's next upgrade — #519

D-CLOUD-182 makes controlled device alignment and the relevant migration/mutation-residue disposition a prerequisite for that handheld's next update transfer/reboot. #519 owns the exact plan, old-consumer isolation, synthetic rehearsal, named authorized actions and state-bound acceptance; #516 supplies relevant private residue classification. Alignment cannot be deferred until after replacement firmware is installed. Host builds, public/clean synthetic QA and the existing #515 -> #508 -> #507 source order proceed independently. No personal payload replacement or cloud relocation is inferred.


## Active source-coverage fix — #520

#520 is a child of #515 and must qualify before #508 integration and #507 scope freeze. Full packaged writer chains confirm ordinary PPSSPP savedata, DuckStation memory cards and standalone Mupen64Plus save states can be omitted by current save rules or misclassified as ROM content. Correct coverage in place, including backup/restore, content copy/match/list/count and bounded validator consumers; preserve supported existing layouts. Synthetic old-source failure and fixed-source byte-preservation controls plus affected actual VM presentation proof are in progress. This is not consent to relocate saves or clean private clouds.


## Additional confirmed writer gap — #521

Child #521 qualifies DuckStation default screenshot placement. The exact packaged screenshot action/writer and shipped VM/H700 seeds resolve ordinary captures outside the saves tree. Correct new default capture placement while preserving explicit custom paths and all historical captures; source-derived launcher controls and target-runtime proof accompany the change. This is a separate scoped fix before #508/#507, not a general reorganization feature or permission to move personal files.


## DuckStation runtime prerequisite — #522

Actual GENERIC_X64 proof for #521 found the exact pinned AppImage installed mode0644; direct execution refuses with126. #522 fixes explicit package executable mode and proves original/fixed install behavior plus real target entrypoint execution. It precedes #521 screenshot runtime acceptance. Preserve the source/cache bytes and persistent saves; no guest-only chmod is a product fix. Include this input in #508 integration and #507 scope.
